course.title: Voice Training and Diction
course.tagline: Train a clear, strong voice: breathing, pronunciation and presence.

days.title: Meet your voice
days.goal: Know how your voice works.

video.title: 1 121 12321 Scale Exercise | Diction & Pitch Vocal Training for Singers

steps: Watch today's video and follow the warm-up for how your voice works: breath, vocal cords, mouth exactly as shown.
Do the how your voice works: breath, vocal cords, mouth exercise for 10 minutes, breathing from your belly, not your chest.
Read a short paragraph aloud three times, applying how your voice works: breath, vocal cords, mouth each time.
Record yourself reading and listen back for clarity, pace and breath.
Use how your voice works: breath, vocal cords, mouth in a real conversation or recording today and notice the difference.
days.task: Hum a note and feel the buzz in your throat and chest.
days.challenge: Record your voice reading a paragraph. Listen back.

quiz.q: What makes your voice?
options: Air from your lungs passing over your vocal cords.
Your throat alone.
Your mouth alone.
Your nose alone.
quiz.explain: Your voice is air from your lungs passing over your vocal cords. Breath is the fuel of your voice.

quiz.q: Which of these is the goal of today's lesson?
options: Record your voice and hear how you sound.
Know how your voice works.
Let your feelings show in your voice.
Use your chest voice for power.
quiz.explain: Today's lesson is about Meet your voice — its goal is: Know how your voice works.

quiz.q: Which of these did today's lesson focus on?
options: speaking clearly: saying every sound
changing your pitch: high and low notes
sounding clear on the phone
how your voice works: breath, vocal cords, mouth
quiz.explain: Today's focus was how your voice works: breath, vocal cords, mouth.

options: breathing from your belly
opening your mouth wider when you speak
pronouncing tricky sounds clearly
changing your speed to fit your message
